name: Developmental Motor Delay and Early Screening
summary: Motor delay means a child achieves motor milestones later than expected. It may be isolated, part of global developmental delay, or a sign of a specific condition (CP, neuromuscular disease, genetic syndromes).

looksLike: Late milestones, "floppy" or stiff baby, asymmetry, persistent hand preference before about 12 months (suggests weakness on the other side), clumsiness, frequent falls, difficulty with handwriting or sport.

book.title: Developmental Motor Delay and Early Screening

blocks.text: Motor delay means a child achieves motor milestones later than expected. It may be isolated, part of global developmental delay, or a sign of a specific condition (CP, neuromuscular disease, genetic syndromes). **Developmental** **coordination disorder (DCD)** is a condition in which motor coordination is significantly below expected for age, affecting daily life and school, not explained by another condition.

sections.title: G. RED FLAGS AND URGENT CONDITIONS

rows: Waddling gait, difficulty rising from the floor using hands on legs (Gowers sign), large calves in a boy
Marked hypotonia with weakness, poor feeding, weak cry
Neuromuscular disease (for example spinal muscular atrophy)
Head circumference abnormal or growing rapidly

steps: **Delay identified with a validated tool?** Refer for medical assessment to find the cause, and start early intervention.
**Early intervention:** parent-coached, play-based motor practice in daily routines.
**DCD:** task-oriented training (for example CO-OP or neuromotor task training) [Ref – to verify].

items: Coach parents to embed practice in play: tummy time, reaching games, supported sitting, cruising along furniture. Task-oriented, goal-based practice for older children: ball skills, bike riding, handwriting with occupational therapy. Promote physical activity and participation in sport for confidence and fitness.
**Why correct age for prematurity?** Milestones should be judged by corrected age in early years.
**What is the Gowers sign?** Using hands to "climb up" the legs when rising from the floor, indicating proximal weakness.
**Why is early hand preference concerning?** It may reflect weakness on the other side.
**What is DCD?** A coordination disorder significantly affecting daily activities, not explained by another condition.
**Best approach for DCD?** Task-oriented training focused on the child's goals.

sections.title: Now You Should Be Able To

items: Recognise motor delay and red flags.

sections.A: Motor delay ka matlab hai bachcha motor milestones (baithna, chalna) umeed se der se haasil karta hai. Yeh akela ho sakta hai ya kisi aur masle ka hissa.
sections.B: Der se milestones, dheela ya akda bachcha, ek taraf ka farq, aur bohat jaldi ek haath ki pasand.
sections.D: Umar ke mutabiq tools: AIMS (0-18 mahine), General Movements Assessment aur doosre validated tests.
sections.G: Seekhi hui salahiyat khatam hona, ya batakh jaisi chaal aur zameen se uthne mein mushkil: refer.
sections.H: Red flags hon to refer. Validated tool se delay mile to wajah ke liye medical assessment, aur saath mein early intervention.
sections.I: Maa baap ko sikhayein ke khel mein practice kaise karwayein: tummy time, haath barhane wale khel, sahara de kar baithna aur cruising.
sections.N: Sawaal hal karein. Qabl az waqt paida bachchon mein milestones corrected age se dekhein.
sections.now-you-should-be-able-to: Yeh checklist hai. Har point khud kar sakein to tick karein.
